newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch sees economic rebound late this year.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch sees economic rebound late this year.

text.p: New Zealand's Finance Minister Bill Birch said in a speech on Tuesday he believed a rebound in economic growth would start late in 1997 on the back of interest rate falls earlier this year.

"The rebound, starting late this year, will be kick-started by previous cuts in interest rates, which are already down three percentage points on their level in October 1996," Birch said in the text of a speech due to be delivered in Dunedin.

Birch noted that the new Monetary Conditions Index, which forms a guide for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's ideal level of monetary tightness, had been cut by 100 basis points on Friday, in effect sanctioning the market-led easing to date.
"Interest rates, both short and long-term, are now slightly under 7.0 percent and the trade-weighted exchange rate has settled below 67," Birch told the Otago Chamber of Commerce.

The government has been arguing for several months that lower interest rates, a steadier exchange rate, a low inflation outlook and the prospect of a stronger world economy would all work to improve business conditions during this year.
